title: STAC-GNSS
subtitle: Spatiotemporal Learning of Open-Pit Slope Deformation from Sparse GNSS Networks
question: How can sparse GNSS observations be used to reconstruct and forecast the continuous spatiotemporal deformation of a large slope system?
context: The project investigates long-term three-dimensional GNSS displacement observations distributed across multiple zones of a large open-pit slope. The focus is the relationship between discrete monitoring points and continuous slope deformation.
progress: Current focus includes adaptive graph learning, spatial relationships, continuous deformation fields, multi-horizon forecasting, spatial holdout and cross-zone generalization.
direction: The broader objective is not simply to predict displacement at individual sensors, but to investigate whether sparse monitoring networks contain sufficient information for AI to learn the evolving state of a continuous geosystem.
next: GNSS + InSAR + terrain + environmental observations → multimodal representation → spatial generalization → physics-constrained dynamics.
update: The 26 August 2026 progress report describes a TRCQ-GNSS framework: asynchronous history encoding, propagation on a fixed terrain graph and continuous spatial queries. It reports 7/30/90-day three-dimensional forecasting with strict time splits and hidden-station evaluation. This is recorded here as a dated research update; the STAC-GNSS project identity is retained. The reported application is stable to slowly deforming conditions within the same mine. Sudden acceleration and cross-mine transfer require further validation.
outputs: Research framework and ongoing evaluation. Public paper, code and data are forthcoming.
